value.body: A two-year master's degree in computer applications covering programming, data structures, databases, networks, software engineering and electives such as data science, cloud or cybersecurity. It is a common route into software jobs for graduates from BCA, B.Sc and other non-engineering backgrounds.

items.label: Course length
items.note: 4 semesters; AICTE cut it from 3 years from 2020-21

items.label: Students enrolled
items.note: All modes, including ~35,000 in distance mode

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree such as BCA, B.Sc, B.Com or B.A., usually with Mathematics at Class 12 or graduation level (exact rules vary by institute). NITs and some IIITs admit through NIMCET; central universities such as DU and BHU use CUET-PG; states run their own tests (MAH-MCA-CET, TS/AP ICET, TANCET, KMAT and others); many universities hold their own test or admit on marks.

value.title: At a glance
items: The Mathematics requirement rules out some B.Com and B.A. graduates — check each institute's eligibility.
Most graduates go into software development, testing, data and IT services roles.
MCA graduates can take UGC-NET (Computer Science) or GATE for teaching or further study.

value.title: MCA enrolment
value.note: All modes of study (regular, distance, private). AISHE counts responding institutions only; coverage varies by year.
value.source: AISHE 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24, Table 11 programme-wise enrolment, actual responses (Ministry of Education)
